seo.title: Audit Engagement Checklist for Smart Contract Auditors
seo.description: Complete smart contract audit methodology from scoping to report delivery. 75+ items covering security reviews used by professional audit firms.

content.intro: A complete audit methodology checklist covering every phase of a professional smart contract security review - from initial scoping to final report delivery. Used by top audit firms.

sections.heading: Pre-Engagement Phase
sections.description: Initial scoping and preparation before the audit begins.

items.title: Define audit scope and deliverables
items.description: Document all contracts in scope, lines of code, and expected deliverables. Clarify what's out of scope.

items.title: Gather project documentation
items.description: Collect whitepapers, architecture docs, previous audits, and design specifications from the client.

items.title: Identify external dependencies
items.description: List all oracles, external protocols, and third-party contracts the system interacts with.

items.title: Establish communication channels
items.description: Set up secure channels for questions, findings disclosure, and progress updates.

items.title: Review previous audit reports
items.description: Study any prior audits to understand historical issues and verify fixes.

items.title: Set up development environment
items.description: Clone repo, install dependencies, ensure all tests pass, set up debugging tools.

items.title: Identify key invariants with team
items.description: Discuss critical properties that must always hold - these become primary audit targets.

items.title: Map trust assumptions
items.description: Document what roles are trusted, what external systems are trusted, and failure assumptions.

sections.heading: Architecture Review
sections.description: High-level analysis of system design and threat model.

items.title: Map contract inheritance hierarchy
items.description: Diagram inheritance relationships and identify diamond/multiple inheritance issues.

items.title: Analyze access control model
items.description: Document all privileged roles, their capabilities, and how permissions can change.

items.title: Review upgrade mechanisms
items.description: Analyze proxy patterns, upgrade timelock, and storage collision risks.

items.title: Map external call graph
items.description: Document all cross-contract calls and potential reentrancy entry points.

items.title: Analyze economic model
items.description: Understand token flows, fee mechanisms, and economic invariants.

items.title: Review oracle integration design
items.description: Analyze price feed sources, staleness handling, and manipulation resistance.

items.title: Document state machine transitions
items.description: Map all possible states and valid transitions for stateful contracts.

items.title: Identify centralization risks
items.description: Document admin keys, multisig requirements, and potential single points of failure.

items.title: Review all external/public functions
items.description: Analyze each entry point for input validation, access control, and state changes.

items.title: Trace ETH and token flows
items.description: Follow all value transfers to verify accounting accuracy and prevent fund loss.

items.title: Analyze arithmetic operations
items.description: Check for overflow/underflow, rounding errors, and precision loss.

items.title: Review loop bounds and gas limits
items.description: Identify unbounded loops that could cause DoS via gas exhaustion.

items.title: Check reentrancy guards
items.description: Verify CEI pattern or reentrancy locks on all external calls.

items.title: Analyze storage layouts
items.description: Check for slot collisions in upgradeable contracts and packed struct issues.

items.title: Review error handling
items.description: Verify appropriate use of require/revert, custom errors, and error messages.

items.title: Check event emissions
items.description: Verify all state changes emit appropriate events for off-chain tracking.

items.title: Run static analyzers (Slither, Mythril)
items.description: Execute static analysis tools and triage all findings.

items.title: Execute symbolic execution (Manticore)
items.description: Use symbolic execution to explore edge cases and constraint violations.

items.title: Run fuzzing campaigns
items.description: Set up Echidna or Foundry fuzzing with property-based tests.

items.title: Perform formal verification checks
items.description: Use Certora or Halmos for critical invariant verification.

items.title: Analyze gas optimization opportunities
items.description: Identify expensive operations and suggest optimizations.

items.title: Check code coverage
items.description: Ensure test suite covers all branches and edge cases.

items.title: Run dependency audit
items.description: Check imported libraries for known vulnerabilities.

items.title: Verify compiler settings
items.description: Check Solidity version, optimizer settings, and via-IR usage.

items.title: Test flash loan attack vectors
items.description: Attempt price manipulation, governance attacks, and liquidity drainage via flash loans.

items.title: Analyze oracle manipulation resistance
items.description: Test TWAP effectiveness, multi-oracle fallbacks, and manipulation costs.

items.title: Check MEV extraction risks
items.description: Identify sandwich attack vectors, frontrunning opportunities, and backrunning risks.

items.title: Test liquidation mechanics
items.description: Verify liquidation thresholds, incentives, and cascade prevention.

items.title: Analyze interest rate models
items.description: Test use curves, rate jumps, and economic stability.

items.title: Check slippage protections
items.description: Verify deadline parameters, minimum output amounts, and price bounds.

items.title: Test deposit/withdrawal edge cases
items.description: Check first depositor attacks, rounding exploits, and share inflation.

items.title: Analyze governance attack vectors
items.description: Test vote buying, flash loan voting, and proposal spam attacks.

sections.heading: Integration Testing
sections.description: Testing contract interactions with external systems.

items.title: Test mainnet fork scenarios
items.description: Run integration tests against forked mainnet state with real protocol data.

items.title: Verify cross-chain bridge interactions
items.description: Test message passing, finality assumptions, and bridge failure handling.

items.title: Test oracle failure scenarios
items.description: Simulate stale prices, oracle downtime, and manipulation attempts.

items.title: Verify upgrade path correctness
items.description: Test storage migrations, initialization, and rollback scenarios.

items.title: Test emergency procedures
items.description: Verify pause mechanisms, emergency withdrawals, and circuit breakers.

items.title: Analyze composability risks
items.description: Test interactions with other DeFi protocols and potential conflicts.

items.title: Test gas under network congestion
items.description: Verify critical functions work within block gas limits during high gas periods.

items.title: Verify off-chain component integration
items.description: Test keeper bots, relayers, and off-chain computation correctness.

items.title: Classify severity accurately
items.description: Use consistent severity ratings: Critical, High, Medium, Low, Informational.

items.title: Write clear reproduction steps
items.description: Provide PoC code or step-by-step instructions to reproduce each finding.

items.title: Explain impact clearly
items.description: Describe worst-case scenarios, affected users, and potential fund loss.

items.title: Provide actionable recommendations
items.description: Suggest specific code changes or architectural improvements.

items.title: Link to relevant references
items.description: Reference similar past exploits, documentation, or security guidelines.

items.title: Track finding status
items.description: Maintain status tracking: Open, Acknowledged, Fixed, Won't Fix.

items.title: Document mitigating factors
items.description: Note any factors that reduce severity or exploitability.

items.title: Cross-reference related findings
items.description: Link findings that share root causes or have combined impact.

sections.heading: Report Delivery
sections.description: Finalizing and delivering the audit report.

items.title: Conduct internal peer review
items.description: Have findings reviewed by another auditor before client delivery.

items.title: Verify fix implementations
items.description: Review all fixes and confirm they address the root cause without introducing new issues.

items.title: Update finding statuses
items.description: Mark all findings as Fixed, Partially Fixed, Acknowledged, or Disputed.

items.title: Write executive summary
items.description: Summarize overall security posture, key risks, and recommendations.

items.title: Document audit limitations
items.description: Clearly state scope boundaries, time constraints, and what wasn't reviewed.

items.title: Provide deployment recommendations
items.description: Suggest monitoring, incident response, and post-deployment security measures.

items.title: Schedule final walkthrough
items.description: Review findings with client team and answer technical questions.

items.title: Archive audit materials
items.description: Securely store PoCs, notes, and tooling output for future reference.

proTips: Build a personal vulnerability checklist: Maintain your own list of patterns based on past audits and public exploits. Update it after every engagement.
Read the code multiple times with different lenses: First pass for understanding, second for logic errors, third for edge cases, fourth for economic attacks.
Always question trust assumptions: Admin keys get compromised, oracles fail, external protocols get hacked. Test what happens when trusted components misbehave.
Write PoCs for every medium+ finding: A working exploit removes all doubt about severity and helps clients prioritize fixes.
Study past exploits weekly: Follow rekt.news, DeFiHackLabs, and post-mortems. Most vulnerabilities are variations of known patterns.

seo.title: DeFi Code Review Checklist
seo.description: Peer review checklist for DeFi protocol code changes. Covers financial logic, oracles, MEV protection, and integration safety.

content.intro: A detailed code review checklist specifically for DeFi protocols. Use this when reviewing PRs for lending protocols, DEXs, yield aggregators, and other financial smart contracts.

items.title: Verify interest rate calculations
items.description: Check compound interest formulas, accrual frequency, and precision handling.

items.title: Check exchange rate calculations
items.description: Verify share/asset conversions. Look for rounding direction vulnerabilities.

items.title: Review fee calculations and distribution
items.description: Verify fee percentages, recipients, and collection timing.

items.title: Validate collateral ratio math
items.description: Check liquidation thresholds, LTV calculations, and health factor formulas.

items.title: Verify reward distribution logic
items.description: Check reward accrual, claiming, and vesting calculations.

items.title: Check for precision loss in divisions
items.description: Review order of operations. Multiply before divide to preserve precision.

items.title: Validate slippage calculations
items.description: Verify slippage tolerance is applied correctly in swaps.

items.title: Review decimal handling for different tokens
items.description: Verify handling of 6-decimal (USDC), 8-decimal (WBTC), and 18-decimal tokens.

sections.heading: Oracle Integration
sections.description: Review price feed usage and manipulation resistance.

items.title: Verify oracle staleness checks
items.description: Confirm stale price detection with appropriate thresholds per asset.

items.title: Check for oracle manipulation vectors
items.description: Assess if prices can be manipulated within a single transaction.

items.title: Review TWAP implementation if used
items.description: Verify TWAP window is long enough to resist manipulation.

items.title: Check fallback oracle logic
items.description: Verify behavior when primary oracle fails or returns invalid data.

items.title: Verify price decimal normalization
items.description: Ensure oracle prices are correctly scaled for calculations.

items.title: Check round ID validation (Chainlink)
items.description: Verify answeredInRound >= roundId for fresh data.

items.title: Review price bounds/circuit breakers
items.description: Verify extreme price movements trigger protection mechanisms.

items.title: Check for oracle front-running risks
items.description: Assess if oracle updates create arbitrage or attack opportunities.

sections.heading: Liquidity & Solvency
sections.description: Verify protocol remains solvent under all conditions.

items.title: Check for bad debt scenarios
items.description: Verify liquidation incentives ensure positions are closed before underwater.

items.title: Review withdrawal queue logic
items.description: Check handling of insufficient liquidity for withdrawals.

items.title: Verify use rate calculations
items.description: Ensure interest rates respond appropriately to use.

items.title: Check first depositor attack resistance
items.description: Verify initial share minting doesn't allow share manipulation.

items.title: Review share inflation attacks
items.description: Check for donation attacks that inflate share value.

items.title: Verify reserve factor collection
items.description: Check that protocol reserves are correctly accumulated.

items.title: Check for dust attack vectors
items.description: Verify small amounts don't cause DoS or accounting issues.

items.title: Review emergency liquidity mechanisms
items.description: Verify circuit breakers and emergency withdrawal paths.

items.title: Identify sandwich attack vectors
items.description: Check if user transactions can be profitably sandwiched.

items.title: Review frontrunning opportunities
items.description: Identify transactions that leak profitable information.

items.title: Check deadline parameter usage
items.description: Verify swaps/operations have expiration timestamps.

items.title: Verify slippage protection
items.description: Confirm minimum output amounts are enforced correctly.

items.title: Review liquidation ordering
items.description: Check if liquidation ordering can be gamed for MEV.

items.title: Check for JIT liquidity vulnerabilities
items.description: Assess if just-in-time liquidity can exploit users.

items.title: Review backrunning opportunities
items.description: Identify if large trades create backrunning value.

items.title: Consider private mempool usage
items.description: For sensitive operations, recommend Flashbots or similar.

sections.heading: Access Control & Governance
sections.description: Review permission systems and admin functions.

items.title: Review all admin-only functions
items.description: Verify admin capabilities are documented and limited appropriately.

items.title: Check timelock on parameter changes
items.description: Sensitive parameters should have timelock delays.

items.title: Verify role separation
items.description: Different functions should require different roles.

items.title: Review upgrade mechanisms
items.description: Check proxy patterns, storage layouts, and upgrade auth.

items.title: Check emergency pause functionality
items.description: Verify pause scope, who can trigger, and unpause process.

items.title: Review guardian/multisig requirements
items.description: Critical functions should require multiple signers.

items.title: Check for centralization risks
items.description: Identify single points of failure or excessive admin power.

items.title: Verify parameter bounds
items.description: Admin-settable parameters should have sensible limits.

items.title: Check reentrancy on external calls
items.description: Verify CEI pattern or reentrancy guards on all external calls.

items.title: Review token approval handling
items.description: Check for approval race conditions and infinite approvals.

items.title: Verify callback handler security
items.description: If implementing callbacks (flash loans), verify caller validation.

items.title: Check for composability assumptions
items.description: Document assumptions about integrated protocols.

items.title: Review flash loan integration
items.description: If using flash loans, verify proper repayment and callback security.

items.title: Check for read-only reentrancy
items.description: Verify view functions can't be manipulated via reentrancy.

items.title: Verify cross-protocol assumptions
items.description: Check assumptions about external protocol behavior.

items.title: Review token standard edge cases
items.description: Check handling of fee-on-transfer, rebasing, and non-standard tokens.

sections.heading: Testing & Documentation
sections.description: Verify code quality and test coverage.

items.title: Check test coverage for changes
items.description: New code should have detailed tests including edge cases.

items.title: Verify fuzzing for financial functions
items.description: Mathematical operations should be fuzz tested.

items.title: Review integration test scenarios
items.description: Complex user flows should have end-to-end tests.

items.title: Check invariant tests
items.description: Protocol invariants should be tested with property-based tests.

items.title: Verify NatSpec documentation
items.description: All public functions should have complete documentation.

items.title: Review change documentation
items.description: PR should explain what changed and why.

items.title: Check for gas optimizations needed
items.description: High-frequency functions should be gas efficient.

items.title: Verify event emissions
items.description: State changes should emit appropriate events.

proTips: Always trace the math by hand: For any financial calculation, work through specific examples manually before trusting the code.
Think like an attacker with a flash loan: Ask: What could I do with unlimited capital in a single transaction? This catches most DeFi bugs.
Check edge cases: zero, one, max: Every numeric input should be tested with 0, 1, and type(uint256).max.
Review rounding direction for every division: Rounding should favor the protocol, not users. Inconsistent rounding is exploitable.
Draw the token flow diagram: For complex operations, diagram where tokens move. Missing flows mean lost or stuck funds.

seo.title: Dapp Launch Checklist for Frontend Developers
seo.description: Production dapp launch checklist for Web3 frontends. Covers wallet integration, transaction handling, error states, and deployment.

content.intro: The complete checklist for launching a decentralized application frontend. Covers wallet integration, transaction handling, error states, security, and production deployment.

items.title: Support all major wallets
items.description: MetaMask, WalletConnect, Coinbase Wallet, Rainbow at minimum.

items.title: Handle wallet not installed gracefully
items.description: Show installation links when wallet extension is missing.

items.title: Persist connection across sessions
items.description: Remember connected wallet. Auto-reconnect on page load.

items.title: Support mobile wallet browsers
items.description: Test in MetaMask mobile, Trust Wallet, and Coinbase Wallet browsers.

items.title: Handle account changes correctly
items.description: React to accountsChanged event. Update UI and refetch data.

items.title: Handle chain changes correctly
items.description: React to chainChanged event. Prompt network switch if wrong chain.

items.title: Implement clean disconnect flow
items.description: Clear connection state and cached data on disconnect.

items.title: Show connected wallet address
items.description: Display truncated address and ENS name if available.

items.title: Show clear transaction preview
items.description: Display what will happen before user signs. Show amounts, recipients.

items.title: Estimate gas accurately
items.description: Show estimated gas cost in native token and USD.

items.title: Handle pending state correctly
items.description: Show loading indicator, disable retry, display pending toast.

items.title: Track transaction confirmation
items.description: Poll for receipt. Update UI when confirmed.

items.title: Handle transaction failure gracefully
items.description: Parse error messages. Show user-friendly failure reason.

items.title: Provide block explorer links
items.description: Link to Etherscan/explorer for transaction details.

items.title: Handle user rejection
items.description: Detect when user cancels in wallet. Reset UI appropriately.

items.title: Support transaction speed-up/cancel
items.description: Allow users to speed up or cancel pending transactions.

items.title: Handle RPC errors
items.description: Catch and display RPC failures. Offer retry option.

items.title: Handle insufficient funds
items.description: Check balance before enabling actions. Show clear message.

items.title: Handle insufficient allowance
items.description: Detect when approval is needed. Guide user through approval.

items.title: Handle contract reverts
items.description: Parse revert reasons. Display human-readable error.

items.title: Handle network congestion
items.description: Suggest higher gas when transaction is stuck.

items.title: Handle stale data
items.description: Show loading states. Prevent actions on outdated data.

items.title: Handle offline state
items.description: Detect offline. Show appropriate message and disable actions.

items.title: Implement global error boundary
items.description: Catch unexpected errors. Show recovery option.

sections.heading: Security & Safety
sections.description: Protect users from attacks and mistakes.

items.title: Validate all user inputs
items.description: Sanitize addresses, amounts, and other inputs.

items.title: Verify contract addresses
items.description: Hardcode or validate contract addresses. Never trust URL params.

items.title: Show transaction simulation results
items.description: Use Tenderly or similar to show expected outcome.

items.title: Warn on high slippage
items.description: Alert users when slippage exceeds safe thresholds.

items.title: Implement phishing protection
items.description: Show domain verification. Warn about suspicious sites.

items.title: Secure API keys
items.description: Use environment variables. Never expose private keys in frontend.

items.title: Validate network before transactions
items.description: Confirm user is on correct chain before sending.

items.title: Rate limit sensitive operations
items.description: Prevent rapid-fire transactions that could drain wallets.

items.title: Configure RPC fallbacks
items.description: Multiple RPC providers with automatic failover.

items.title: Implement request caching
items.description: Cache contract reads. Use SWR or React Query.

items.title: Optimize bundle size
items.description: Tree-shake unused code. Lazy load heavy components.

items.title: Set up CDN and caching
items.description: Use CDN for static assets. Configure cache headers.

items.title: Implement loading skeletons
items.description: Show placeholder content during data fetching.

items.title: Test under poor network conditions
items.description: Verify app works on slow/unstable connections.

items.title: Set up error monitoring
items.description: Use Sentry or similar for production error tracking.

items.title: Monitor RPC usage and costs
items.description: Track API calls. Optimize to reduce costs.

items.title: Update contract addresses for mainnet
items.description: Switch from testnet to mainnet contract addresses.

items.title: Configure production RPC endpoints
items.description: Use paid RPC services for reliability.

items.title: Enable production analytics
items.description: Set up Mixpanel, Amplitude, or custom analytics.

items.title: Verify CSP and security headers
items.description: Configure Content Security Policy to prevent XSS.

items.title: Test production build thoroughly
items.description: Full end-to-end testing on production deployment.

items.title: Set up IPFS backup
items.description: Deploy to IPFS for censorship-resistant hosting.

items.title: Configure custom domain
items.description: Set up domain, SSL, and DNS correctly.

items.title: Monitor uptime
items.description: Set up uptime monitoring and alerts.

proTips: Test with real wallets on testnet first: Don't rely only on local testing. Real wallets behave differently.
Parse every possible error type: Users blame your app, not their wallet. Make errors crystal clear.
Cache aggressively, invalidate correctly: Balance between fast UI and accurate data. Invalidate on tx confirmation.
Support hardware wallets explicitly: Ledger and Trezor have different flows. Test them specifically.
Build for mobile-first: More users access dapps via mobile wallets than desktop extensions.

seo.title: Solana Program Deployment Checklist
seo.description: Solana program deployment checklist covering Anchor builds, authority management, and mainnet launch. 50+ items for production readiness.

content.intro: The complete Solana program deployment checklist from final testing through mainnet deployment. Covers Anchor-specific steps, upgrade authority management, and production monitoring.

sections.heading: Final Code Review
sections.description: Last checks before building for production.

items.title: All tests passing on localnet and devnet
items.description: Run `anchor test` and integration tests. Verify all instructions work correctly.

items.title: Remove all msg! debug logging
items.description: Debug logs consume compute units. Search for and remove all msg! statements.

items.title: Verify program ID in declare_id!
items.description: Confirm the declared program ID matches your deployment keypair.

items.title: Check compute unit budget
items.description: Ensure all instructions fit within 200K CU limit. Profile heavy operations.

items.title: Verify account size calculations
items.description: Check all account space allocations include discriminator (8 bytes for Anchor).

items.title: Audit signer and authority checks
items.description: Verify every instruction validates required signers and authorities.

items.title: Review PDA seeds for uniqueness
items.description: Ensure PDA seeds create unique addresses. Avoid seed collisions.

items.title: Confirm all security audit findings fixed
items.description: Review audit report. All critical and high issues must be resolved.

items.title: Set verifiable build in Anchor.toml
items.description: Enable `[programs.localnet]` with verifiable = true for reproducible builds.

items.title: Configure correct cluster in Anchor.toml
items.description: Set cluster to mainnet-beta for production deployment.

items.title: Verify Rust and Solana CLI versions
items.description: Document exact versions used. Match audited build environment.

items.title: Build with --verifiable flag
items.description: Run `anchor build --verifiable` for reproducible bytecode.

items.title: Check program binary size
items.description: Verify.so file is under size limits. Optimize if needed.

items.title: Generate and verify IDL
items.description: Build IDL with `anchor idl init`. Verify it matches program interface.

items.title: Document build hash
items.description: Record SHA256 of deployed.so file for verification.

items.title: Prepare deployment keypairs
items.description: Have program keypair and upgrade authority keypair ready and backed up.

sections.heading: Devnet Final Testing
sections.description: Complete testing on devnet before mainnet.

items.title: Deploy to devnet with production config
items.description: Use identical build and configuration as planned mainnet deployment.

items.title: Run full integration test suite
items.description: Execute all user flows against devnet deployment.

items.title: Test upgrade path
items.description: If upgradeable, test full upgrade process including data migration.

items.title: Verify client SDK works correctly
items.description: Test TypeScript/Rust client against devnet deployment.

items.title: Test error handling paths
items.description: Verify all error conditions return correct error codes.

items.title: Measure transaction costs
items.description: Profile SOL costs for all instructions. Document for users.

items.title: Test with production RPC
items.description: Use mainnet RPC provider against devnet to verify connection.

items.title: Verify event/log parsing
items.description: Confirm off-chain services correctly parse program logs.

items.title: Fund deployment wallet
items.description: Ensure deployer has enough SOL for deployment and buffer account rent.

items.title: Deploy program to mainnet
items.description: Run `anchor deploy` or `solana program deploy` with correct keypairs.

items.title: Upload IDL to chain
items.description: Run `anchor idl init` to store IDL on-chain for explorers.

items.title: Verify deployment on explorer
items.description: Check Solscan/Solana Explorer. Confirm program data account.

items.title: Record deployment transaction
items.description: Document deployment signature, slot, and timestamp.

items.title: Verify upgrade authority
items.description: Confirm upgrade authority is set to intended address (multisig).

items.title: Initialize required accounts
items.description: Create any global state accounts or config PDAs.

items.title: Configure program parameters
items.description: Set fees, limits, and other configurable parameters.

items.title: Transfer upgrade authority to multisig
items.description: Use `solana program set-upgrade-authority` to move to Squads multisig.

items.title: Verify multisig configuration
items.description: Confirm multisig threshold, signers, and timelock settings.

items.title: Document authority addresses
items.description: Public documentation of upgrade authority and any admin keys.

items.title: Test authority functions
items.description: Verify admin functions work with new authority.

items.title: Set up authority monitoring
items.description: Alert on any upgrade authority changes or program upgrades.

items.title: Plan upgrade process
items.description: Document exact steps for future program upgrades.

items.title: Consider making immutable
items.description: For mature programs, consider removing upgrade authority entirely.

items.title: Back up all keypairs securely
items.description: Store program keypair and authority keys in secure cold storage.

sections.heading: Post-Deployment
sections.description: Verify deployment and set up monitoring.

items.title: Execute smoke tests on mainnet
items.description: Run basic operations with small amounts to verify functionality.

items.title: Verify all PDAs are accessible
items.description: Confirm all program-derived addresses resolve correctly.

items.title: Test frontend with mainnet
items.description: Full end-to-end test of application with production deployment.

items.title: Set up transaction monitoring
items.description: Configure alerts for failed transactions and unusual patterns.

items.title: Monitor program logs
items.description: Set up log aggregation for debugging and analytics.

items.title: Configure error alerting
items.description: Alert on specific error codes indicating security issues.

items.title: Update documentation
items.description: Publish program address, IDL, and integration guides.

items.title: Schedule security monitoring
items.description: Set up ongoing security reviews and monitoring.

proTips: Always use verifiable builds: Verifiable builds let anyone confirm deployed bytecode matches source. Essential for trust.
Deploy program first, then transfer authority: Easier to fix deployment issues before authority is with multisig.
Keep your program keypair forever: Even after transferring upgrade authority, you need the keypair to prove program ownership.
Use priority fees during congestion: Deployment transactions can fail during high activity. Add priority fees for reliability.
Test IDL parsing with Anchor clients: An IDL mismatch between client and program is a common source of integration bugs.

seo.title: Smart Contract Deployment Checklist
seo.description: Pre-mainnet deployment checklist for Solidity smart contracts. Covers testing, configuration, access control, and production monitoring.

content.intro: The definitive pre-deployment checklist for Solidity developers. From final code review to mainnet deployment, this guide ensures nothing is missed when real money is on the line.

sections.heading: Final Code Review
sections.description: Last checks before freezing the code.

items.title: All tests passing with 100% of critical paths covered
items.description: Run full test suite. Ensure all edge cases for value transfers and state changes are tested.

items.title: Remove all console.log and debug code
items.description: Search for console.log, hardhat/console.sol imports, and test-only functions.

items.title: Verify correct Solidity version
items.description: Use a stable, audited compiler version. Avoid floating pragmas (^0.8.0).

items.title: Check optimizer settings
items.description: Document optimizer runs. Higher runs = cheaper execution, larger bytecode.

items.title: Verify contract sizes under 24KB
items.description: Check bytecode size limits. Split contracts or use libraries if needed.

items.title: Remove unused imports and dead code
items.description: Clean up any code that isn't used in production paths.

items.title: Verify NatSpec documentation is complete
items.description: All public/external functions should have @notice, @param, and @return docs.

items.title: Confirm audit findings are resolved
items.description: All critical and high findings must be fixed. Medium issues should be addressed or documented.

sections.heading: Configuration & Parameters
sections.description: Verify all deployment parameters are correct.

items.title: Verify constructor arguments
items.description: Double-check all addresses, rates, and configuration values. Use checksummed addresses.

items.title: Confirm admin/owner addresses
items.description: Owner should be a multisig, not an EOA. Verify multisig signers and threshold.

items.title: Set appropriate timelock delays
items.description: Critical operations should have 24-48 hour timelocks minimum.

items.title: Verify oracle addresses and feeds
items.description: Confirm Chainlink feed addresses are correct for target network.

items.title: Check fee parameters and limits
items.description: Verify fee percentages, max fees, and fee recipient addresses.

items.title: Confirm token addresses and decimals
items.description: Verify all token addresses. Check decimals handling for non-18 decimal tokens.

items.title: Set initial rate limits
items.description: Configure conservative limits for withdrawals, mints, and other operations.

items.title: Document all magic numbers
items.description: Every constant should be documented with its meaning and rationale.

items.title: Deploy multisig wallet first
items.description: Create Safe or other multisig with appropriate signers before contract deployment.

items.title: Set up role-based access control

seo.title: Blockchain Client Security Checklist
seo.description: Security checklist for blockchain engineers covering consensus safety, P2P security, node operations, and protocol implementation.

content.intro: Blockchain infrastructure has unique security requirements. A single bug in consensus or networking can compromise the entire network. This checklist covers critical areas.

items.description: Incorrect fork choice can cause chain splits or stuck nodes.
Blocks marked final must actually be final. Reorging finalized blocks breaks assumptions.
Validators must be slashed for violations. Missing slashing allows attacks.
System must tolerate f Byzantine nodes with 3f+1 total nodes.
Clock drift between nodes must not break consensus.
Boundary conditions between slots and epochs are bug-prone.
Verify peer identity. Prevent impersonation attacks.
Ensure node connects to diverse peers. Detect isolation attempts.
Rate limit messages. Disconnect misbehaving peers.
Validate all P2P messages before acting on them.
Track peer behavior. Penalize and disconnect bad actors.
Support nodes behind NAT. Use hole punching or relays.
All transaction signatures must be verified. Missing checks allow forgery.
Nonces must be sequential. Gaps or repeats indicate bugs.
Incorrect gas can cause DoS or allow free execution.
Limit mempool size. Prevent spam transactions.
Same inputs must produce same ordering. Nondeterminism causes consensus failures.
State roots must be calculated identically across clients.
Pruning must not remove data needed for validation.
Clients should detect and recover from database corruption.
When syncing state, verify proofs. Do not trust peers blindly.
Historical data must remain accessible and correct.
Never implement cryptography yourself. Use established libraries.
Timing attacks can leak private keys. Use constant-time comparisons.
Use cryptographically secure RNG. Weak randomness breaks security.
Validator keys must be encrypted at rest and in memory when possible.
Use modern hash functions. Be aware of collision attacks.
Admin RPC endpoints must require authentication.
Logs must not contain secrets. Metrics endpoint should be internal.
Software updates must be signed and verified.
Memory, disk, and connection limits prevent resource exhaustion.
Only necessary ports exposed. Admin interfaces internal only.

sections.heading: Protocol Upgrades
sections.description: Handle hard forks and upgrades safely.

items.description: Test fork transitions on testnet thoroughly before mainnet.
Have ability to roll back if upgrade causes issues.
Coordinate upgrades across multiple client teams.
If upgrade changes state format, migration must be correct.

commonMistakes.impact: Different clients compute different state, causing network split.
commonMistakes.prevention: Ensure all operations are deterministic. No floating point, no random.

commonMistakes.impact: Malicious peers can feed false data and corrupt local state.
commonMistakes.prevention: Always verify proofs. Never trust, always verify.

commonMistakes.impact: Network can be brought down by spam.
commonMistakes.prevention: Rate limiting, peer scoring, message validation at every layer.

commonMistakes.impact: Implementation bugs lead to key leaks or signature forgery.
commonMistakes.prevention: Use audited libraries. Have cryptographic implementations reviewed.

proTips: Run the checklist against your CI pipeline, not just before release.
Track which items have caught real issues to prioritize your review effort.
Pair checklist reviews with automated linting where possible.

seo.title: DeFi Security Checklist for Developers
seo.description: A detailed security checklist for DeFi developers covering AMMs, lending, vaults, and cross-protocol integrations. Ship secure DeFi code.

content.intro: DeFi protocols handle significant value and face sophisticated attackers. Use this checklist to ensure your protocol is hardened against known attack vectors before deployment.

sections.heading: Oracle Security
sections.description: Protect against price manipulation and oracle failures.

items.title: Use TWAP or manipulation-resistant oracles
items.description: Avoid spot prices from DEXes. Use Chainlink, time-weighted averages, or other manipulation-resistant sources.

items.title: Implement oracle staleness checks
items.description: Reject prices older than acceptable threshold. Include updatedAt timestamp validation.

items.title: Add oracle fallback mechanisms
items.description: If primary oracle fails, have a secondary source or safe fallback behavior.

items.title: Validate oracle price bounds
items.description: Reject prices that deviate too far from expected ranges to catch oracle manipulation.

items.title: Check oracle decimals handling
items.description: Chainlink feeds have different decimals. Normalize all price feeds to consistent precision.

items.title: Protect against oracle front-running
items.description: Consider commit-reveal or other mechanisms if oracle updates create arbitrage opportunities.

items.title: Use TWAP instead of spot prices
items.description: Flash loans cannot manipulate time-weighted averages. Never rely on single-block spot prices.

items.title: Add deposit/withdraw delays where needed
items.description: For governance or rewards, consider requiring deposits to be present for multiple blocks.

items.title: Check same-block deposit-and-action restrictions
items.description: Prevent users from depositing and taking action (voting, claiming) in the same block.

items.title: Validate share price manipulation resistance
items.description: Vault share prices should not be manipulable by large deposits/withdrawals in single transactions.

items.title: Consider flash loan fees in arbitrage calculations
items.description: Understand that attackers pay fees. Some attacks are unprofitable after fees.

items.title: Verify constant product/sum invariant maintained
items.description: After every operation, the pool invariant must hold. Test edge cases thoroughly.

items.title: Protect against sandwich attacks
items.description: Implement slippage protection and consider private transaction submission options.

items.title: Check minimum liquidity requirements
items.description: First LP should lock minimum liquidity to prevent share price manipulation.

items.title: Validate fee calculation accuracy
items.description: Fees must be calculated correctly in all scenarios including edge cases.

items.title: Test imbalanced pool scenarios
items.description: Verify behavior when pools become highly imbalanced or near-empty.

items.title: Check LP token mint/burn accounting
items.description: LP tokens must accurately represent share of pool. No inflation or deflation bugs.

items.title: Verify health factor calculations
items.description: Health factor must be calculated correctly including all positions and proper oracle prices.

items.title: Check liquidation thresholds and incentives
items.description: Liquidation must be profitable enough to incentivize liquidators but not excessive.

items.title: Protect against bad debt scenarios
items.description: Have mechanisms to handle underwater positions where debt exceeds collateral.

items.title: Verify interest rate model
items.description: Interest accrual must be calculated correctly. Test with various use levels.

items.title: Check borrow cap enforcement
items.description: Borrow limits must be enforced to prevent protocol insolvency.

items.title: Test partial liquidation scenarios
items.description: Partial liquidations must leave positions in valid state or fully liquidate.

sections.heading: Vault and Yield Security
sections.description: For vaults, yield aggregators, and staking.

items.title: Protect against first depositor attack
items.description: Send small amount to vault on deployment or implement virtual shares to prevent share inflation attack.

items.title: Validate share price calculations
items.description: Share price must accurately reflect underlying assets. Check for rounding attacks.

items.title: Check donation attack resistance
items.description: Donating tokens to vault should not unfairly benefit or harm depositors.

items.title: Verify withdrawal queue handling
items.description: If using withdrawal queues, ensure fair processing and no front-running.

items.title: Check yield strategy risks
items.description: Understand and document risks of underlying yield sources. Implement loss limits.

items.title: Implement emergency withdrawal
items.description: Users should be able to withdraw in emergencies even if it means forfeiting some yield.

sections.heading: Token Integration Security
sections.description: Handle edge cases with various token implementations.

items.title: Use SafeERC20 for all token transfers
items.description: Some tokens don't return bool. SafeERC20 handles these edge cases.

items.title: Handle fee-on-transfer tokens
items.description: Calculate actual received amount after transfer, not the transfer amount.

items.title: Handle rebasing tokens
items.description: Account for balance changes between transactions for tokens like stETH.

items.title: Check token decimal handling
items.description: Normalize calculations for tokens with different decimals (USDC has 6, DAI has 18).

items.title: Verify approval patterns
items.description: Use increaseAllowance/decreaseAllowance or reset to zero first for tokens with approval race conditions.

items.title: Handle tokens with blocklists
items.description: USDC and USDT can blocklist addresses. Consider implications for your protocol.

sections.heading: Economic Security
sections.description: Protect against economic exploits and incentive manipulation.

items.title: Model economic attacks
items.description: Think through how an attacker with unlimited capital could exploit your protocol.

items.title: Verify fee and reward math
items.description: All fee distributions must sum correctly. No funds should be lost or created.

items.title: Check for MEV extraction opportunities
items.description: Identify where sandwich attacks, front-running, or back-running could harm users.

items.title: Validate incentive alignment
items.description: Ensure all protocol participants are incentivized to behave honestly.

items.title: Test extreme market conditions
items.description: Simulate behavior during high volatility, black swan events, and market crashes.

proTips.tip: Always get an audit before mainnet deployment. DeFi protocols are high-value targets.
Study past exploits deeply. Most new exploits are variations of known attack patterns.
Deploy to mainnet with limited caps first. Increase limits as the protocol proves itself.
Set up monitoring and alerts for unusual activity. Early detection limits damage.
Have an incident response plan ready before you need it. Know who to call and what to do.

seo.title: GameFi Security Checklist
seo.description: Security checklist for GameFi developers covering smart contract integration, asset security, economy protection, and game-specific vulnerabilities.

content.intro: GameFi combines traditional game security with blockchain security. This checklist covers critical security areas unique to Web3 games.

items.description: All game contracts should be audited before mainnet deployment.
If contracts are upgradeable, protect the upgrade admin with multisig and timelock.
Use Chainlink VRF or commit-reveal for randomness. Block hash is predictable.

items.task: Reentrancy protection on all external calls
items.description: Use checks-effects-interactions or reentrancy guards on mint/transfer functions.
Use Solidity 0.8+ or SafeMath for all arithmetic.
Only authorized addresses can mint, modify stats, or change game parameters.
Decide if metadata is mutable. If mutable, restrict who can change it.
Understand that on-chain royalties are not always enforceable on all marketplaces.
Protect against accidental burns. Consider requiring confirmation.
Ensure assets cannot be duplicated through contract bugs.
If assets bridge chains, ensure bridge is secure and verified.
Limit how many tokens can be minted per time period to prevent inflation exploits.
Prevent rapid reward claiming that could drain pools.
If using on-chain voting or prices, consider flash loan manipulation.
If using price oracles, ensure they cannot be easily manipulated.
Large instant withdrawals could indicate an exploit. Add delays or limits.
Detect and prevent automated farming that destroys economy.
Never trust the client for game outcomes, loot, or economic actions.
Verify all blockchain transactions through your backend before accepting.

items.task: Private keys never in client code
items.description: Admin or treasury keys must never be embedded in game clients.
Memory editing, speed hacks, and automation should be detected.
Obfuscate client code to slow down reverse engineering.
Use WalletConnect, Web3Modal, or other standard connection methods.
Users should understand what they are signing. Clear transaction descriptions.
Request only the approvals needed. Avoid unlimited approvals.
Warn users about phishing. Provide official links and verification.
If using embedded wallets, implement proper session timeout and re-auth.
Prevent API abuse through rate limiting per user and IP.
Admin APIs require authentication and are not publicly accessible.
Player data and game state should be encrypted in storage.
API keys, private keys, and secrets use proper secrets management.
Log suspicious activity and set up alerts for anomalies.

commonMistakes.impact: Miners can manipulate results. Players can predict outcomes.
commonMistakes.prevention: Use Chainlink VRF or commit-reveal schemes.

commonMistakes.impact: Cheaters can modify client to claim any reward.
commonMistakes.prevention: Server-authoritative architecture for all economic actions.

commonMistakes.impact: Exploits can hyperinflate token supply and destroy economy.
commonMistakes.prevention: Rate limits, caps, and monitoring on all minting.

commonMistakes.mistake: Storing admin keys in client config
commonMistakes.impact: Anyone decompiling client gets admin access.
commonMistakes.prevention: Admin keys stay server-side only. Use multisig.

proTips: Playtest with real users before auditing - they will find exploits your checklist misses.
Separate game logic security from token security in your review.
Test reward distribution under extreme load - that is where most GameFi bugs appear.

seo.title: NFT Smart Contract Security Checklist
seo.description: A detailed security checklist for NFT developers covering minting, metadata, royalties, and marketplace integration. Launch secure NFT collections.

content.intro: NFT contracts face unique security challenges around minting, metadata, and marketplace integration. Use this checklist to secure your collection before launch.

sections.heading: Minting Security
sections.description: Secure the minting process against common exploits.

items.title: Enforce maximum supply limit
items.description: Verify that minting cannot exceed the advertised maximum supply under any circumstances.

items.title: Protect against reentrancy during mint
items.description: Use ReentrancyGuard on mint functions to prevent callback-based minting exploits.

items.title: Validate mint price cannot be bypassed
items.description: Ensure msg.value check cannot be bypassed and excess ETH is handled properly.

items.title: Limit mints per wallet
items.description: Implement per-wallet limits and verify they cannot be bypassed via contract calls.

items.title: Verify allowlist Merkle proof implementation
items.description: Check Merkle tree implementation for vulnerabilities. Use OpenZeppelin's MerkleProof.

items.title: Prevent signature replay attacks
items.description: If using signatures for allowlists, include nonces and expiration timestamps.

items.title: Check for integer overflow in quantity mints
items.description: Batch mint quantity multiplied by price must not overflow.

sections.heading: Token ID and Randomness
sections.description: Secure token ID assignment and reveal mechanics.

items.title: Use verifiable randomness for reveals
items.description: Use Chainlink VRF or commit-reveal scheme. Block hash is predictable by miners.

items.title: Protect against reveal sniping
items.description: Prevent minters from predicting which token ID they will receive before reveal.

items.title: Verify provenance hash implementation
items.description: Provenance hash should be committed before mint starts and verifiable after reveal.

items.title: Check for token ID enumeration issues
items.description: Verify token IDs are assigned correctly without gaps or collisions.

items.title: Secure batch reveal logic
items.description: If revealing in batches, ensure each batch cannot influence future batch outcomes.

sections.heading: Metadata Security
sections.description: Secure metadata storage and URI handling.

items.title: Pin metadata to IPFS or use permanent storage
items.description: Use IPFS pinning service or Arweave to prevent metadata loss. Centralized servers are a rug risk.

items.title: Freeze metadata after reveal
items.description: Lock baseURI after reveal to prevent post-mint metadata manipulation.

items.title: Validate tokenURI implementation
items.description: Ensure tokenURI returns correct URI for all valid token IDs and reverts for invalid ones.

items.title: Check for URI injection vulnerabilities
items.description: If constructing URIs dynamically, ensure no injection of malicious paths.

items.title: Verify contractURI for marketplace compatibility
items.description: Implement contractURI for collection-level metadata on OpenSea and other marketplaces.

sections.heading: Royalties and Fees
sections.description: Implement royalties correctly for marketplace compatibility.

items.title: Implement EIP-2981 royalty standard
items.description: Use EIP-2981 for on-chain royalty info. Most marketplaces check this standard.

items.title: Validate royalty percentage bounds
items.description: Royalty percentage should be capped at reasonable level (typically 10% max).

items.title: Set royalty receiver correctly
items.description: Royalty receiver should be an address you control. Consider using a splitter contract.

items.title: Consider operator filter for royalty enforcement
items.description: Implement OpenSea's Operator Filter Registry if you want to enforce royalties on supporting marketplaces.

items.title: Test royalty calculation with various sale prices
items.description: Verify royalty math works correctly for both small and large sale amounts.

items.title: Protect owner/admin functions
items.description: All administrative functions must have appropriate access control modifiers.

items.title: Use Ownable2Step for ownership transfers
items.description: Two-step ownership transfer prevents accidental lockout from typos.

items.title: Limit what owner can change post-mint
items.description: Owner should not be able to change critical parameters that could rug holders.

items.title: Consider renouncing ownership after launch
items.description: For fully decentralized collections, consider renouncing ownership after setup.

items.title: Implement withdrawal function for stuck funds
items.description: Have a way to withdraw ETH and accidentally sent tokens from the contract.

items.title: Implement all required ERC-721 functions
items.description: balanceOf, ownerOf, safeTransferFrom, transferFrom, approve, setApprovalForAll, getApproved, isApprovedForAll must all work correctly.

items.title: Emit required events
items.description: Transfer, Approval, and ApprovalForAll events must be emitted correctly.

items.title: Implement ERC-165 supportsInterface
items.description: Return true for ERC721, ERC721Metadata, and ERC165 interface IDs.

items.title: Handle safeTransferFrom correctly
items.description: Must call onERC721Received on recipient contracts and revert if not accepted.

items.title: Check zero address handling
items.description: Transfers to zero address should revert. Burning should use a burn function.

items.title: Use efficient ERC-721 implementation
items.description: Consider ERC721A for batch minting efficiency. It significantly reduces gas for multiple mints.

items.title: Minimize storage writes
items.description: Pack storage variables efficiently. Use uint96 for token counters if under max.

items.title: Optimize string operations
items.description: Pre-compute string concatenations where possible. Avoid dynamic string operations.

items.title: Test gas costs at various mint quantities
items.description: Verify gas costs are acceptable for single and batch mints.

items.title: Consider lazy minting for large collections
items.description: For very large collections, consider minting on demand rather than batch minting.

proTips.tip: Test on OpenSea Testnets before mainnet. Marketplace compatibility issues are common.
Use ERC721A for collections expecting batch mints. The gas savings are substantial.
Always verify your contract on Etherscan immediately after deployment.
Keep 10-20% of supply for team, marketing, and unexpected issues. Running out causes problems.
Have a communication plan ready for launch issues. Discord and Twitter must be monitored.

seo.title: Security Vulnerability Checklist for Smart Contract Auditors
seo.description: A detailed audit checklist covering all vulnerability classes, from reentrancy to access control. Use this systematic approach to ensure thorough coverage.

content.intro: This checklist provides a systematic approach to smart contract auditing. Work through each category methodically to ensure no vulnerability class is overlooked.

sections.heading: Pre-Audit Setup
sections.description: Essential preparation before starting the code review.

items.title: Review project documentation and specifications
items.description: Read the whitepaper, technical docs, and understand the intended behavior before looking at code.

items.title: Identify scope and out-of-scope contracts
items.description: Confirm exactly which contracts are in scope and document any dependencies that are out of scope.

items.title: Set up local development environment
items.description: Clone the repo, install dependencies, and ensure tests pass before starting review.

items.title: Run automated analysis tools
items.description: Execute Slither, Mythril, and other static analysis tools to get an initial vulnerability report.

items.title: Create a contract architecture diagram
items.description: Map out contract interactions, inheritance, and external dependencies visually.

sections.heading: Access Control Checks
sections.description: Verify all authorization and permission mechanisms.

items.title: Verify all external/public functions have appropriate access control
items.description: Every function that modifies state should have explicit access restrictions unless intentionally open.

items.title: Check for missing onlyOwner or role modifiers
items.description: Administrative functions must be protected. Look for functions that should be restricted but aren't.

items.title: Audit role-based access control implementation
items.description: If using roles, verify proper role assignment, revocation, and role hierarchy logic.

items.title: Check for centralization risks
items.description: Identify single points of failure where one compromised key could drain funds or break the protocol.

items.title: Verify two-step ownership transfer
items.description: Critical ownership changes should require acceptance to prevent accidental lockout.

items.title: Review timelock and governance constraints
items.description: Check if administrative actions are properly timelocked for user protection.

sections.heading: Reentrancy Analysis
sections.description: Check for all types of reentrancy vulnerabilities.

items.title: Verify checks-effects-interactions pattern
items.description: All state changes must happen before external calls. No state updates after external calls.

items.title: Check for ReentrancyGuard on sensitive functions
items.description: Functions making external calls should use reentrancy protection, especially those handling value.

items.title: Analyze cross-function reentrancy
items.description: Check if an attacker could re-enter through a different function that shares state with the vulnerable function.

items.title: Check cross-contract reentrancy
items.description: Analyze if reentrancy is possible through calls to other contracts in the same protocol.

items.title: Review read-only reentrancy risks
items.description: Check if view functions return stale data during reentrancy that other protocols might rely on.

items.title: Test ERC-777 and ERC-1155 callback hooks
items.description: If accepting arbitrary tokens, verify protection against token callback reentrancy.

sections.heading: Arithmetic and Logic
sections.description: Verify mathematical operations and business logic.

items.title: Check for overflow/underflow in unchecked blocks
items.description: Solidity 0.8+ has overflow protection, but unchecked blocks bypass it. Verify intentional use.

items.title: Verify division and rounding behavior
items.description: Check if rounding favors the protocol or user, and if it can be exploited through dust amounts.

items.title: Test precision loss in calculations
items.description: Multiply before divide to minimize precision loss. Check for cases where order matters.

items.title: Verify percentage and fee calculations
items.description: Check that fees are calculated correctly and cannot exceed 100% or cause unexpected behavior.

items.title: Check for division by zero
items.description: All division operations should be protected against zero denominators.

items.title: Validate boundary conditions
items.description: Test behavior at max/min values, empty arrays, zero amounts, and other edge cases.

sections.heading: External Interactions
sections.description: Review all interactions with external contracts and users.

items.title: Verify return values from external calls
items.description: Check that return values from external calls are validated, especially for token transfers.

items.title: Check for unsafe ERC-20 transfers
items.description: Use SafeERC20 or check return values. Some tokens don't return bool on transfer.

items.title: Validate oracle data freshness
items.description: Check that oracle prices have staleness checks and fallback mechanisms.

items.title: Review flash loan attack vectors
items.description: Analyze if price manipulation or large position changes via flash loans could be exploited.

items.title: Check for force-sending ETH attacks
items.description: Contracts relying on balance checks can be manipulated via selfdestruct force-send.

items.title: Verify callback handling
items.description: If implementing callbacks (like uniswapV3SwapCallback), verify caller authentication.

sections.heading: Protocol-Specific Checks
sections.description: Checks specific to DeFi protocol types.

items.title: For AMMs: Check for price manipulation
items.description: Verify that spot prices cannot be manipulated to extract value from the protocol.

items.title: For lending: Verify liquidation math
items.description: Check that liquidations properly handle edge cases and cannot be griefed or blocked.

items.title: For vaults: Check share manipulation
items.description: Verify first depositor cannot inflate share price to grief subsequent depositors.

items.title: For staking: Verify reward distribution
items.description: Check that rewards cannot be claimed multiple times or drained by flash deposits.

items.title: For bridges: Verify message validation
items.description: Check that cross-chain messages are properly validated and cannot be replayed.

items.title: For NFTs: Check minting limits and randomness
items.description: Verify that minting cannot exceed supply and randomness cannot be manipulated.

sections.heading: Gas and DoS
sections.description: Check for denial of service and gas-related issues.

items.title: Identify unbounded loops
items.description: Loops over arrays that can grow indefinitely may cause out-of-gas failures.

items.title: Check for block gas limit issues
items.description: Functions processing many items may exceed block gas limit as usage grows.

items.title: Verify push over pull patterns
items.description: Use pull payments instead of push to prevent recipient-controlled failures.

items.title: Check for griefing via failed external calls
items.description: Verify that a failing external call cannot block critical protocol functions.

items.title: Review gas cost variability
items.description: Check if gas costs can vary dramatically based on input, enabling gas griefing.

sections.heading: Upgrade and Proxy Safety
sections.description: For upgradeable contracts, verify upgrade safety.

items.title: Check storage layout compatibility
items.description: New implementation must be storage-compatible with previous version. No reordering variables.

items.title: Verify initializer protection
items.description: Initializers must only run once. Check for reinitializer if needed for upgrades.

items.title: Check for uninitialized implementation
items.description: Implementation contract should be initialized or made non-initializable to prevent takeover.

items.title: Verify upgrade authorization
items.description: Only authorized parties should be able to upgrade. Check for timelock on upgrades.

items.title: Test function selector clashes
items.description: Proxy admin functions must not clash with implementation function selectors.

proTips.tip: Start with the highest-value functions (those handling the most funds) and work outward.
Keep a running list of potential issues during first pass, then investigate each thoroughly.
Write proof-of-concept exploits for all medium+ severity findings. If you can't exploit it, reconsider the severity.
Review similar protocol audits for context. Past vulnerabilities in comparable code are likely to reappear.
Document your findings as you go. Waiting until the end often means missing details you noticed early.

seo.title: Smart Contract Security Checklist for Solidity Developers
seo.description: A detailed security checklist for Solidity developers to audit their smart contracts before deployment. Covers reentrancy, access control, and more.

content.intro: This security checklist covers the most critical vulnerabilities and best practices every Solidity developer should verify before deploying a smart contract. Use it as your pre-deployment audit guide to catch issues before they become exploits.

sections.heading: Reentrancy Protection
sections.description: Reentrancy is one of the most common and dangerous vulnerabilities. Ensure all external calls are protected.

items.title: Use ReentrancyGuard on all external-facing functions
items.description: Apply OpenZeppelin's ReentrancyGuard or implement checks-effects-interactions pattern on any function that makes external calls.

items.title: Follow checks-effects-interactions pattern
items.description: Always update state variables before making external calls. Never update state after external calls.

items.title: Audit cross-function reentrancy
items.description: Check if an attacker can re-enter through a different function that shares state with the vulnerable function.

items.title: Review read-only reentrancy risks
items.description: View functions called by other protocols can return stale data during reentrancy. Mark state-changing functions appropriately.

items.title: Check ERC-777 token callbacks
items.description: If your contract interacts with arbitrary ERC-20s, ensure you're protected against ERC-777 callbacks.

items.title: Verify ERC-721/1155 callback safety
items.description: onERC721Received and onERC1155Received can be reentrancy vectors. Protect accordingly.

items.title: Review flashloan interaction safety
items.description: If your contract can be called within a flashloan, ensure all invariants hold within a single transaction.

items.title: Test with Foundry invariant tests
items.description: Write invariant tests that attempt reentrancy during fuzzing to catch edge cases.

items.title: Document reentrancy assumptions
items.description: Add NatSpec comments explaining which functions are reentrancy-safe and why.

items.title: Consider pull-over-push pattern
items.description: Where possible, let users withdraw funds rather than pushing to them automatically.

sections.heading: Access Control
sections.description: Verify that only authorized addresses can call privileged functions.

items.title: Implement role-based access control
items.description: Use OpenZeppelin's AccessControl or Ownable2Step for managing admin permissions.

items.title: Use two-step ownership transfer
items.description: Implement Ownable2Step to prevent accidental ownership loss from typos in transfer.

items.title: Verify all admin functions have modifiers
items.description: Audit every function that should be restricted and ensure proper modifiers are applied.

items.title: Review initializer protection
items.description: For upgradeable contracts, ensure initializers can only be called once and by the deployer.

items.title: Check for missing zero-address validation
items.description: Validate that critical addresses (owner, admin, fee recipient) cannot be set to address(0).

items.title: Implement timelock for sensitive operations
items.description: Add time delays for critical admin functions to give users time to react.

items.title: Review function visibility
items.description: Ensure internal/private functions aren't accidentally exposed as public/external.

items.title: Audit delegatecall targets
items.description: Any delegatecall to user-controlled addresses can be used to hijack the contract.

items.title: Verify constructor/initializer sets owner
items.description: Ensure ownership is properly assigned during deployment, not left as address(0).

items.title: Test access control in all code paths
items.description: Write tests that verify unauthorized users cannot access restricted functions.

sections.heading: Arithmetic & Data Validation
sections.description: Ensure all mathematical operations and input data are handled safely.

items.title: Use Solidity 0.8+ for overflow protection
items.description: Solidity 0.8+ has built-in overflow/underflow checks. For unchecked blocks, verify manually.

items.title: Validate division by zero scenarios
items.description: Check all division operations for potential zero denominators.

items.title: Review precision loss in calculations
items.description: Order operations to minimize precision loss: multiply before divide.

items.title: Validate array bounds
items.description: Ensure array access uses valid indices, especially with user-supplied indices.

items.title: Check for phantom function signatures
items.description: Verify fallback/receive functions don't accidentally catch intended function calls.

items.title: Validate external call return values
items.description: Always check return values from external calls, especially low-level calls.

items.title: Use SafeERC20 for token transfers
items.description: Some tokens don't return booleans. Use SafeERC20 to handle all cases.

items.title: Validate deadline parameters
items.description: If using deadlines, ensure block.timestamp comparisons are correct (< vs <=).

items.title: Check signature malleability
items.description: Use OpenZeppelin's ECDSA library which handles signature malleability.

items.title: Validate chainId for signatures
items.description: Include chainId in EIP-712 signatures to prevent cross-chain replay attacks.

sections.heading: Gas & Economic Security
sections.description: Protect against gas griefing and economic attacks.

items.title: Limit unbounded loops
items.description: Avoid iterating over arrays that can grow unboundedly. Use pagination or caps.

items.title: Set gas limits for external calls
items.description: Use.call{gas: X}() to prevent called contracts from consuming all gas.

items.title: Check for block gas limit DoS
items.description: Ensure no operation can exceed block gas limit, making the contract unusable.

items.title: Validate oracle price freshness
items.description: Check that oracle prices are recent and not stale. Implement heartbeat checks.

items.title: Implement slippage protection
items.description: Allow users to specify minimum output amounts to prevent sandwich attacks.

items.title: Review flashloan attack vectors
items.description: Assume an attacker can borrow unlimited capital in a single transaction.

items.title: Check for front-running vulnerabilities
items.description: Use commit-reveal or private mempools for operations sensitive to ordering.

items.title: Validate fee calculations
items.description: Ensure fee percentages don't overflow and are capped at reasonable values.

items.title: Test with extreme values
items.description: Fuzz test with type(uint256).max and 0 to catch edge cases.

items.title: Review incentive alignment
items.description: Analyze if any actor has incentive to act maliciously. Design for adversarial conditions.

sections.heading: Pre-Deployment Verification
sections.description: Final checks before deploying to mainnet.

items.title: Run Slither static analysis
items.description: Execute 'slither.' and address all high/medium findings.

items.title: Run Foundry invariant tests
items.description: Create and run invariant tests to catch unexpected state violations.

items.title: Achieve 100% branch coverage
items.description: Use 'forge coverage' to ensure all code paths are tested.

items.title: Deploy to testnet first
items.description: Deploy to Sepolia/Goerli and verify behavior matches expectations.

items.title: Verify contract on block explorer
items.description: Publish source code on Etherscan for transparency.

items.title: Document emergency procedures
items.description: Create runbooks for pausing, upgrading, and recovering from incidents.

items.title: Set up monitoring
items.description: Configure alerts for unusual activity using Tenderly, Forta, or OpenZeppelin Defender.

items.title: Review with fresh eyes
items.description: Have a colleague review the code or wait 24 hours before final deployment.

seo.title: ZK Circuit Security Checklist
seo.description: Security checklist for zero-knowledge engineers covering circuit constraints, trusted setup, proof verification, and common ZK vulnerabilities.

content.intro: ZK circuits have unique security concerns. Missing constraints, faulty math, and verification bugs can allow provers to create valid proofs for false statements. This checklist covers critical security areas.

sections.heading: Constraint Completeness
sections.description: Ensure all inputs are properly constrained.

items.description: Every public input must be used in constraints. Unconstrained inputs let provers choose arbitrary values.

items.task: All private inputs contribute to output
items.description: Private inputs must affect the proven statement. Otherwise provers can use any private input.
All intermediate values should be fully determined by inputs. Check for degrees of freedom.

items.task: Range constraints on all numeric inputs
items.description: Field elements wrap around. Ensure values stay in expected ranges.
x * (x - 1) === 0 enforces boolean. Just saying 'is boolean' is not enough.
Array indices must be constrained to valid ranges.
Arithmetic wraps at field modulus. Large numbers can wrap to small ones.
Division by zero is undefined. Ensure denominators are non-zero.
Field elements have two square roots. Constrain which one is expected.
Less-than comparisons are expensive and tricky in circuits. Verify implementation.
When decomposing to bits, ensure reconstruction equals original.
All inputs to hash functions must be constrained. Unconstrained inputs allow hash manipulation.
All signature components verified. Partial verification allows forgery.
The message being signed must be part of the signature verification constraints.
Verify public keys are valid curve points. Invalid keys can cause issues.
Nullifiers must be uniquely derived. Multiple nullifiers for same input allow double-spending.
Each Merkle path direction must be constrained boolean.
Final hash must equal claimed root. Check hash ordering at each level.
The leaf value must include all relevant data, not just identifiers.
Circuit tree depth must match actual tree depth.
Define what empty leaves hash to. Ensure consistency.
Use parameters from a multi-party ceremony. Single-party setups are trusted.
Circuit must fit within the powers of tau size used in setup.
Verification key must match the deployed circuit exactly.

items.task: No reuse of proving keys for different circuits
items.description: Each circuit needs its own setup. Never reuse keys across circuits.
Verifier must be generated from same circuit used by prover.
Public input ordering must match between prover and verifier.
Include nonce or timestamp in public inputs to prevent replay.
Verifier must reject malformed proofs, not revert or panic.
On-chain verification must fit within block gas limits.

sections.heading: Application Logic
sections.description: How ZK proofs integrate with application.

items.description: Proofs should include action-specific data to prevent misuse.
Proofs should have time bounds to prevent indefinite validity.
Spent nullifiers must be recorded. Missing check allows double-spend.
Data from oracles or other sources must be validated before use in proofs.

commonMistakes.impact: Provers can claim any public output regardless of private inputs.
commonMistakes.prevention: Audit every public input. Ensure each one appears in at least one constraint.

commonMistakes.impact: Large numbers wrap around, breaking expected logic.
commonMistakes.prevention: Add range checks. Be aware of your field size.

commonMistakes.mistake: Wrong hash ordering in Merkle proofs
commonMistakes.impact: Invalid proofs could be accepted for non-existent leaves.
commonMistakes.prevention: Test with known Merkle roots. Verify left/right ordering.

commonMistakes.impact: Nullifier in one context might collide with another.
commonMistakes.prevention: Include domain separator in nullifier derivation.

proTips: Verify constraint counts match expected values for every circuit change.
Test with adversarial inputs, not just happy-path cases.
Keep the trusted setup ceremony documented and auditable.
